note:
Malcolm, 2026-09-10: replaces the safety-dossier brief for the EU Cosmetics Regulation block — 'a close up shot of an inspector looking at the blue liquid in a lab glassware or doing tests in a laboratory'. The dossier round is superseded, not deleted.

BRIEFED AS THE PARTNER TO A CHOSEN IMAGE, NOT ON ITS OWN. Malcolm picked `STD-GMP-inspector-plant / gpt_image` for the GMP block and the two sit SIDE BY SIDE in the same row, so this frame is directed to match it rather than to be good in isolation. Read off the winner: white hooded coverall with a face mask and clear goggles, BLUE NITRILE GLOVES as the only colour anywhere in the frame, brushed steel, a dark plant with a wet reflective floor, cool desaturated palette, and small distant practical lights falling away behind. All of that is repeated here, and the blue liquid then rhymes with the gloves instead of fighting them — blue stays the single accent across both pictures.

SUBJECT SITS LEFT AND LOOKS RIGHT, deliberately. The GMP winner has its inspector on the RIGHT of frame facing LEFT. This block renders in the LEFT column with GMP on the right, so mirroring the direction turns the two figures inward toward each other rather than both staring off the same edge.

2048x1360 EXACTLY, to match the chosen partner. This matters more than usual: multi-column renders a block image at its NATURAL aspect ratio with no wrapper and no object-fit, so two different ratios would render as two different column heights. Note that on the previous wave nbp_pro and nbp_flash silently returned 4:3 and Luma 16:9 against an explicit 3:2 request — whatever wins here gets normalised to 1.506 before upload rather than trusted.

⚠️ FLUX.2 WILL PROBABLY FAIL THIS ONE. It renders printed graduation digits on laboratory glassware on every glassware wave this project has run, despite being negated by name every time, and it is the only engine that does. On the dossier wave it also drew a legible table of numbered rows on a page about regulatory compliance. It is included per the all-suppliers rule, but check its candidates at full size and expect to discard.

THE LIQUID IS SPECIFIED, NOT NAMED. Every engine's default for an unspecified liquid is milky white, so the blue is described as clear, luminous and transparent with the glass and the light behind it visible THROUGH the column of liquid — a checkable property rather than the adjective 'blue'. The tone is the brand's clinical blue rather than a lurid chemistry-set colour.

NO BRANDING AND NO TEXT ANYWHERE, so no reference is sent and this stays Class B reference-free material.

slots.title: EU Cosmetics Regulation — inspector examining a blue solution
slots.prompt: Editorial photograph, landscape, close on a quality inspector testing a cosmetic formulation in a dark laboratory at night. She stands slightly left of centre, turned three quarters toward the right of the frame, wearing a white hooded coverall with the hood up, a white face mask and clear protective goggles, so her face is largely covered and her whole attention is on the glassware. Her raised hand, in a blue nitrile glove, holds a plain clear glass beaker up to eye level, and she is looking directly at it. The beaker is filled about two thirds with a clear, luminous, completely transparent blue solution — a deep clinical blue with real light in it, and the light source behind is plainly visible THROUGH the column of liquid, so it reads as transparent fluid rather than paint, with a bright meniscus line at its surface and a soft blue caustic thrown onto her glove where the light passes through. Her other gloved hand rests on the bench below holding a slim glass stirring rod. The beaker and her glove are the sharp point of the picture. Behind her the laboratory falls away into darkness: out-of-focus steel shelving, the soft shapes of further plain glassware, and small distant practical lights receding, so the room clearly continues beyond the light. The ground is deep graphite #1A1A1A and it is a real room with depth and air, never a backdrop. Cool desaturated palette throughout of graphite, steel, white coverall and blue — the blue of the liquid and of her gloves is the ONLY colour anywhere in the frame. Lighting is low and motivated: one hard cool key from camera-left raking the beaker so the liquid glows from within, one dim cool fill on the shadow side. Everything is scrupulously clean and in order. 85mm at f2.8, shallow depth of field with the beaker and the near glove sharp and the background well dissolved, fine film grain, quiet and serious, expensive.
